name: TeamStarWolf - The Year 2001 in Intrusions
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. ATT&CK Enterprise techniques that the verified 2001 record supports: the 37 CERT/CC advisories CA-2001-01 to CA-2001-37 and the 15 incident notes IN-2001-01 to IN-2001-15 (ramen, the BIND kits, snmpXdmid and Carko, sadmind/IIS, Code Red and Code Red II, Nimda, Sircam, Kaiten on null sa passwords, the SSH1 CRC-32 exploitation and the year's mass mailers), Microsoft's MS01 bulletins (the bogus VeriSign code-signing certificates of MS01-017, the IE MIME flaw of MS01-020, MS01-033 and MS01-044), CAIDA's Code Red measurements and the Justice Department's 2001 records (the Cisco insiders, the PACER billing bypass, the AIPAC defacement indictment, Gorshkov and Ivanov). No 2001 source prints an ATT&CK id: every entry is this study's later mapping. Equation's four group techniques are left out because ATT&CK does not date them. The Maroochy Shire techniques are in the separate ATT&CK for ICS layer navigator/case-studies/chronicle-2001-ics.json. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/CHRONICLE_2001.md. Scores: 70 the source describes the behavior and the study assigns the id, 50 only a Reported source supports the behavior, 40 the mapping is Inferred.

Mass-mailed attachments, not targeted, so the targeted-delivery technique is the closest fit only: Anna Kournikova (12 Feb), Sircam (25 Jul), Nimda (18 Sep), BadTrans (27 Nov), Goner (4 Dec) (basis: Inferred; a later mapping, since no 2001 source prints an ATT&CK id). An impostor obtains two "Microsoft Corporation" certificates from VeriSign (29 and 30 Jan; MS01-017, 22 Mar) (basis: Described; a later mapping, since no 2001 source prints an ATT&CK id). Sources [4][1] refer to the Sources table of case-studies/CHRONICLE_2001.md.

Worm propagation scanning, the closest fit, not pre-targeting reconnaissance: Code Red's random addresses on TCP 80 (19 Jul); rising 22/tcp scans (5 Nov); 1433/tcp scans before Kaiten (27 Nov) (basis: Inferred; a later mapping, since no 2001 source prints an ATT&CK id). Sources [1][2] refer to the Sources table of case-studies/CHRONICLE_2001.md.

The Gorshkov and Ivanov ring steals card and bank data and extorts victims (verdict 9 Oct 2001) (basis: Described; a later mapping, since no 2001 source prints an ATT&CK id). Sources [20][21] refer to the Sources table of case-studies/CHRONICLE_2001.md.
